sources.entry: httpx2 - HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 client with sync and async APIs, maintained by Pydantic (httpx fork).

summary.one_liner: HTTPX is a fully featured Python 3 HTTP client library with sync and async APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support, and an integrated command-line client.
summary.what_it_does: HTTPX provides a requests-style API for making HTTP requests from Python, with both synchronous and async interfaces. It supports HTTP/1.1 by default and HTTP/2 as an optional install. It can send requests directly to WSGI or ASGI applications, and it applies strict timeouts everywhere. The README also lists connection pooling, persistent sessions with cookies, proxy support, streaming downloads, multipart uploads, automatic decompression, and .netrc support. An optional command-line client is available via the httpx[cli] extra.
use_cases: making HTTP requests from Python scripts
calling REST APIs with async code
sending requests to WSGI or ASGI apps in tests
making HTTP requests from the command line
notable: Sync and async interfaces from one library
Direct requests to WSGI and ASGI applications
Integrated command-line client as an optional extra
Fully type annotated with 100% test coverage claimed in README
caveats: HTTP/2 and other features need optional extras installed
The README does not mention the httpx2 fork listed in awesome-python; this summary covers only the encode/httpx README
